text.tspan: Mohar — what happens when Asha makes a health-insurance claim
The simple version. Follow the numbers 1 → 7. Purple = Asha (patient) · Teal = hospital · Yellow = the blockchain "robot judge" · Blue = insurer
She uses her Aadhaar to prove:
The medical record is locked in a
Only Asha holds the key — and
whoever she chooses to share with.
Her phone re-does the maths using
HER OWN copy of the policy.
Only if it all matches, she signs.
A maths proof that says "this claim
under the limit, not claimed before…
A messenger hands the sealed proof
No human reads any medical file.
Money goes to a brand-new address
that only the hospital can open.
Nobody can tell WHICH hospital got
paid — so a cancer hospital's name
before Asha even leaves the hospital.
Asha gives Dr. Meera a key that works for 24 hours.
Every time the doctor looks, it is written in a
public log Asha can read. She can take access
back anytime — the safe simply gets a new lock.
Only government-registered doctors can be added.
A paramedic scans the QR on Asha's phone.
Any 2 of her 3 trusted people (husband, doctor,
sister) must approve. One alone can't unlock it.
Then blood group, allergies & medicines open
for 24 hours — and every look is logged.
Fake hospital? Expired policy? Claiming twice?
Changing the amount? Splitting a big bill?
Signing for the patient? Re-using someone
else's Aadhaar? → the proof can't even be made,
or the robot judge rejects it. Live, every time.
Hiding the diagnosis in a proof isn’t enough if the payment leaks it.
